title: Abba Binyamin
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: [Berakhot 5b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.5b.21) teaches: Abba Binyamin says, “All my days I took care over two things: that my prayer be before my bed, and that my bed be placed between north and south.” He also says [there](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.5b.25) that if two people enter to pray and one starts first and leaves without waiting for his fellow, his prayer is torn up before him. [In Berakhot 6a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.6a.7) he says that a person’s prayer is heard only in the synagogue, citing a verse, etc. At the end of [Jerusalem Talmud Terumot 3:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Terumot.3.3.12), Rabbi Abbahu tells them that it is Abba Pinimon’s opinion. Possibly he is Abba Binyamin.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The Gemara explains “before my bed” as “close to my bed.” [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Berakhot.5b.21.1) understands this as prayer on rising before work or study. The Davidson English interprets it as prayer before going to sleep. [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=771&lang=en) quotes the original wording.
The linked Yerushalmi gives Abba Pinimon. Hyman suggests that he may be Abba Binyamin.
